title: Spray Dryer
model_title: Spray Dryer (Rotary Atomiser, Co-Current, Cyclone Collection)

introduction.definition: A spray dryer converts a liquid (solution, slurry, emulsion) into a dry powder in one step. A high-speed atomiser wheel or nozzle sprays the liquid into hot air in a large chamber; the fine droplets dry in seconds. Powder falls into the cone and fines are recovered from the exhaust air by a cyclone and/or bag filter.
introduction.summary: A spray dryer turns a liquid feed into a dry powder in one step. The liquid is atomised into fine droplets by a fast-spinning wheel or nozzles inside a chamber of hot air; the water evaporates in seconds and the dry particles fall to the cone or are collected from the exhaust air by a cyclone.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Outlet air temperature controls final moisture; higher inlet temperature increases capacity for the same air flow.

temperature.title: Air cools as it evaporates the droplets
temperature.description: Hot inlet air (often ~ 150–250 °C, higher for robust products) meets the spray at the top. Evaporation is very fast because the droplets are tiny (large surface area); the evaporating droplets stay near the wet-bulb temperature, so even heat-sensitive products (milk, enzymes) survive. Outlet air (~ 70–100 °C) sets the final moisture.

foundation: Structure designed for equipment, product and dynamic loads; explosion venting directed to a safe area.
alignment: Align fans, rotary valves and drives; level chambers and beds.
piping: Air/gas ducts with dampers and expansion joints; dust collection (cyclone, bag filter); explosion isolation where required (ATEX/NFPA).
commissioning: Air balance; heat-up curve; water trials then product; check outlet temperature/moisture control and interlocks.

causes: Wet spray reaching walls, high inlet temperature

safety: Dust explosion: venting/suppression, isolation (NFPA 652/654, ATEX); fire detection.

script.narration: This module introduces the Spray Dryer.
A spray dryer converts a liquid (solution, slurry, emulsion) into a dry powder in one step.
A high-speed atomiser wheel or nozzle sprays the liquid into hot air in a large chamber; the fine droplets dry in seconds.
Powder falls into the cone and fines are recovered from the exhaust air by a cyclone and/or bag filter.
Typical applications include milk powder, coffee, food ingredients; detergents, ceramics, pigments; pharmaceuticals and enzymes.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Spray Dryer.
Check outlet temperature, powder moisture and wall deposits.
Inspect atomiser wheel wear and vibration.
Overhaul atomiser; inspect explosion vents.
Watch for wall deposits/burning: brown/burnt powder, fires. Common cause: wet spray reaching walls, high inlet temperature.
Watch for atomiser vibration: trip, noise. Common cause: wheel wear/imbalance.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
